name: ACV Auctions Inc.

profile.description: ACV Auctions operates a digital wholesale marketplace for used vehicles in the United States, connecting dealers and commercial consignors through online auctions and data-driven inspection, plus marketplace services including ACV Transportation, ACV Capital and AI-powered tools such as MAX inventory management and ClearCar consumer appraisal. CEO George Chamoun has led the company since 2016. Q2 2026 revenue was a record $213.9M (+10% YoY), with marketplace GMV roughly flat; full-year 2026 guidance calls for $845M-$855M revenue (+11-13%). Q3 2026 results had not been reported as of the screen date (guidance $219M-$225M). Market cap approximately $1.8B.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): ACV has grown from a dealer-to-dealer app into a multi-revenue marketplace. Marketplace services (transportation, ACV Capital financing and data) made up 41% of Q2 2026 revenue and grew 17% YoY, and total revenue rose from $208.4M in 2020 to $759.6M in 2025 [1][4]. AI Deployment (2/2): AI products ship to customers. Its AI flags known condition risks and guides inspectors before they touch a vehicle, ClearCar provides AI consumer appraisals that generate dealer leads, and MAX is an AI inventory-management suite showcased at Used Car Week 2025 [2]. Market Share (1/2): ACV is a leading digital wholesale marketplace, but Q2 2026 GMV was roughly flat YoY, so no clear share gains are evident [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): AI data tools are described as early in an adoption 'S-curve,' but no named launches with revenue targets were found [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Q2 2026 R&D was $16.6M, or 7.8% of revenue, above traditional auto-auction peers [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): ACV's stated purpose of building a more transparent, trusted digital marketplace for wholesale vehicles is clear about what it does and for whom, but does not express a purpose beyond the transaction [2]. Community Impact (0/2): no distinctive foundation or dollar-quantified community program was found. Employee Retention (0/2): no turnover or tenure data was found; Comparably rates overall culture 3.0/5 across 352 ratings, with the CEO the highest-rated category, and Great Place to Work certified the Dublin office in December 2025 [2]. Insider Buying (1/2): FMP data show 9 open-market insider purchases in Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 against 4 sales, and a February 2026 analysis noted that insiders were buying. Dollar amounts are modest and later quarters show only grants and tax-related disposals [5].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically using growth-sleeve weights (Forward PEG unavailable and excluded; weighted sum 4.65 of 8 = 5.8, rounded to 6). Growth and balance sheet score full marks: D/E of 64.0% (1.00), revenue growth of 10.4% YoY (1.00) and a 29.5% 5-year revenue CAGR ($208.4M in 2020 to $759.6M in 2025, 2x weight, 1.00) [4][6]. Profitability is the weakness: ROE of -15.1% (2x weight) and a profit margin of -7.9% both score 0.00, reflecting a $66.1M GAAP net loss in 2025 and an $8.2M loss in Q2 2026 [4][6]. Forward P/E of 33.9 scores 0.65. Liquidity is about $89M per day, far above the floor [6].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): ACV's marketplace rests on physical work AI cannot replace: in-person vehicle condition inspections, title and arbitration processes, vehicle transportation and dealer floor-plan financing, which make up the fast-growing marketplace-services segment [1][2]. AI mostly strengthens the model by improving inspection accuracy and pricing. The residual risk is that AI-driven pricing and appraisal tools from rivals or OEM platforms narrow ACV's data advantage, and network effects in a flat-GMV market are not guaranteed. No analyst commentary flagging AI as a threat was found [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI underpins ClearCar, MAX and inspection tools, but ACV does not disclose a quantified AI revenue figure, so the tiebreaker point is withheld [2].

infinite_game.summary: ACV is a technology-led disruptor of a legacy physical-auction industry with a stable founder-era CEO who has led since 2016. Its product evolution into transportation, capital and AI data services shows real adaptability. Through Sinek's lens, however, the cause is mostly about winning share from incumbents: it has sued Manheim and ADESA over access to remarketing platforms, its purpose language is transactional, and employee sentiment is only average. It is playing a growth game well, not yet an infinite one.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): ACV talks about bringing transparency and trust to wholesale vehicle trading, which is a real improvement for dealers, but it is framed around marketplace efficiency rather than a future state people would sacrifice for [2]. No evidence shows the purpose being tested through a crisis or shaping a costly strategic choice.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO George Chamoun has led the company for nearly a decade and was named to Automotive News' 2025 All-Stars list. Employees on Comparably rate the CEO as the company's highest-scoring category, and Great Place to Work's Dublin certification credits him with leading with trust and openness [2]. The overall culture score of 3.0/5 and weaker ratings for environment and compensation point to adequate rather than exceptional trust [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): ACV's posture toward incumbents is adversarial. It filed an antitrust lawsuit alleging that Manheim, ADESA and others blocked its access to the AutoIMS remarketing platform [3]. That frames competition as a fight to win rather than a source of self-improvement.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): ACV has broadened from dealer-to-dealer auctions into transportation, financing and AI data products, with marketplace services now 41% of revenue and growing 17% YoY [1]. These moves extend the original marketplace rather than abandon it.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): leadership has kept investing in AI inspection, data products and R&D ($16.6M in Q2 2026) through years of GAAP losses ($66.1M in 2025) rather than cutting to reach profitability sooner [4]. It also took on the industry incumbents in court [3]. Both choices are bold, but they serve growth more than a stated cause.

investment_thesis: ACV is the scaled digital disruptor in U.S. wholesale used-vehicle remarketing. Revenue has compounded at 29.5% a year, from $208.4M in 2020 to $759.6M in 2025, Q2 2026 revenue was a record $213.9M (+10%), and 2026 guidance of $845M-$855M implies 11-13% growth even with flat marketplace GMV [1][4]. The mix is improving toward higher-attach marketplace services (41% of revenue, +17% YoY), while AI inspection, ClearCar and MAX deepen dealer engagement [1][2]. Insider open-market buying in late 2025 and early 2026 and an Inspire Impact Score of 46 (ALIGNED, no negative attributions) add support [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is profitability and volume. ACV remains GAAP-unprofitable (ROE -15.1%, margin -7.9%, 2025 net loss $66.1M), and at 33.9x forward earnings the stock needs margin expansion that has so far been slow [4][6]. Revenue growth depends on fees and services rather than units, with Q2 2026 GMV roughly flat, so a weak used-vehicle cycle could stall growth [1]. Q3 2026 results, guided to $219M-$225M revenue and $21M-$24M adjusted EBITDA, were still pending at the screen date, and the stock has rallied above its 50-day average (about $8.96) to $10.50, raising the bar [1][6]. Ongoing antitrust litigation, both as plaintiff against Manheim and ADESA and as defendant in a bid-rigging class action, adds legal uncertainty [3].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results against guidance of $219M-$225M revenue (+10-13%) and $21M-$24M adjusted EBITDA; a beat would support the $845M-$855M full-year outlook [1]
Continued growth of marketplace services (ACV Transportation and ACV Capital), which grew 17% YoY to 41% of revenue in Q2 2026 and lift revenue per vehicle [1]
Adoption of AI data products (MAX inventory management, ClearCar consumer appraisal) by dealers, which could raise revenue per dealer and stickiness [2]
key_risks: Persistent GAAP losses: a 2025 net loss of $66.1M and Q2 2026 loss of $8.2M leave little cushion if used-vehicle volumes weaken [4]
Flat marketplace GMV in Q2 2026 shows dependence on take-rate and service attach rather than share gains; incumbent auction operators such as Manheim and ADESA could cap volume growth [1][3]
Legal exposure from the Western District of New York bid-rigging class action and ACV's own antitrust suit against Manheim and ADESA [3]
